<reflection>
The second experiment (higher catalyst concentration) improved discrimination: M3 now has the lowest NLL, followed by M9 and M20. However, many mechanisms remain within a narrow NLL range (differences <5), indicating substantial uncertainty. The aim of the second experiment was to amplify nonlinear catalyst effects; it succeeded in elevating M3 but did not sufficiently separate the large group of deactivation and dimerization mechanisms. We need an experiment that probes different kinetic regimes to further distinguish among these candidates.
</reflection>
<hypothesis>
I propose an experiment with low substrate concentration (0.5 M) while keeping catalyst at 0.01 M and no initial product. This condition will emphasize substrate dependence and may reveal substrate inhibition or deactivation effects. At low substrate, mechanisms with substrate inhibition (M7, M11, M16) should show reduced rates relative to linear expectations. Deactivation mechanisms that depend on substrate (M11, M16) may exhibit faster decay. Additionally, dimerization mechanisms (M2, M3, M19) may show different effective orders in catalyst because the substrate-to-catalyst ratio is high (50:1), potentially suppressing dimer formation if substrate competes. This design avoids extreme conditions and explores a new region of concentration space, providing complementary information to the previous runs.
</hypothesis>
